weather.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued November 16 at 11:27AM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Hanford CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Winter Weather Advisory, snow. Additional snow
accumulations up to 5 inches. For the Winter Storm Warning Above 5,
000 feet, heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 2
and 58 inches. Winds gusting as high as 50 mph.

* WHERE...A portion of central California.

* WHEN...For the Winter Weather Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday. For
the Winter Storm Warning, from 4 AM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact the Monday evening and Tuesday
morning commutes. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches.
weather.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 6 feet expected in the surf zone. * WHERE...Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal Counties. * WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, from 6 PM CST this evening through late Thursday night. For the High Surf Advisory, from 2 AM Tuesday to midnight CST Thursday night. * IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Mobile Coastal; Baldwin Coastal

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 16 at 11:27AM CST until November 20 at 12:00AM CST by NWS Mobile AL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
5 to 6 feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, from 6 PM CST this
evening through late Thursday night. For the High Surf
Advisory, from 2 AM Tuesday to midnight CST Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Mobile Coastal; Baldwin Coastal

For the High Rip Current Risk, from 6 AM CST Tuesday through late Thursday night. * IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Escambia Coastal; Santa Rosa Coastal; Okaloosa Coastal

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 16 at 6:56PM CST until November 20 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Mobile AL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to
6 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current
Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and Okaloosa
Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Tuesday to
midnight CST Thursday night. For the High Rip Current Risk,
from 6 AM CST Tuesday through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 10
feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, from 7 PM this evening to
1 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

weather.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow possible. Total snow accumulations between 1 to 2
feet expected above this elevation; accumulations around 4 feet
above 8,000 feet. Winds could gust as high as 45 mph.

* WHERE...A portion of central California.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact daily travel. Gusty winds could
bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and
overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
weather.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. The latest road conditions for the
state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7
to 12 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County and Coastal Broward County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Thursday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Friday. weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 17 at 2:24PM EST until November 20 at 7:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 AM EST Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Winter Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Ice accumulations around a light glaze to a few hundredths of an inch. For Turnagain Pass, periods of heavy snowfall expected, primarily Thursday morning, with snow totals between 7 and 10 inches. * WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), Lower Matanuska Valley, SW Kenai Peninsula, NW Kenai Peninsula, Interior Kenai Peninsula, and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From 9 AM Wednesday to 3 AM AKST Friday. * IMPACTS...Power outages and tree damage are likely due to the ice. Travel could be nearly impossible. The hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday morning commutes. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...An atmospheric river is on track to move across the region starting Wednesday morning. Initially, the thermodynamic profile will support snow for any precipitation that overcomes strong downsloping in lee of the mountains. However, warmer air aloft moves in Wednesday afternoon as surface temperatures climb also. This will transition any light snow in lee of the mountains to a wintry mix of freezing rain and snow. As the warm nose grows in the lower levels, expect a transition to light freezing rain and then eventually to rain by Wednesday evening for the northern Cook Inlet region. This is a warmer system than the previous one, and one of the few opportunities for accumulating snow will be for Turnagain Pass, where 7 to 10 inches will most likely fall before snow transitions to mixed precipitation.

sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of
13 to 17 ft. For the High Surf Advisory, Large breaking waves
of 15 to 18 ft.

afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM Wednesday to

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 12 to 17 ft. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.3 ft of inundation above ground level is likely in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory, Large breaking waves of 15 to 18 ft along the coast from Wednesday afternoon through Thursday afternoon. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Wednesday afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM Wednesday to 10 AM PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM Wednesday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide is expected to be 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 6:45 AM Wednesday and 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10-19 feet, with local sets of 20-22 feet. Peak surf is expected from late Wednesday through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There is a chance for the coastal flood advisory to be extended through later Thursday to cover the secondary high tide in the evening.

location.region: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches

Large breaking waves of 15 to 18 ft along the coast from this
afternoon through Thursday afternoon.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this afternoon.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM today to 10 AM PST
Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM today to 4 PM
PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.3 ft above normal (7.1 ft MLLW) at 6:45 AM
today and 1.2 ft above normal (7.0 ft MLLW) at 7:15 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.3 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
weather.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

conditions.

Stay off of jetties, piers, rocks, and other waterside
infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

weather.instruction:

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Winter Weather Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Mixed precipitation expected. Ice accumulations around a light glaze to a few hundredths of an inch. For Turnagain Pass, periods of heavy snowfall expected, primarily Thursday morning, with snow totals between 7 and 10 inches. * WHERE...Mixed precipitation in Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), Lower Matanuska Valley, and NW Kenai Peninsula; heavy snowfall for Interior Kenai Peninsula and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From 9 AM Wednesday to 3 AM AKST Friday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday morning commutes. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This product was updated to remove SW Kenai Peninsula and correct impact information in the bullet above. An atmospheric river is on track to move across the region starting Wednesday morning. Initially, the thermodynamic profile will support snow for any precipitation that overcomes strong downsloping in lee of the mountains. However, warmer air aloft moves in Wednesday afternoon as surface temperatures climb also. This will transition any light snow in lee of the mountains to a wintry mix of freezing rain and snow. As the warm nose grows in the lower levels, expect a transition to light freezing rain and then eventually to rain by Wednesday evening for the northern Cook Inlet region. This is a warmer system than the previous one, and one of the few opportunities for accumulating snow will be for Turnagain Pass, where 7 to 10 inches will most likely fall before snow transitions to mixed precipitation.

sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 13
to 17 ft. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 18
to 24 ft with up to 30 ft at favored breakpoints along the
coast from this afternoon through Friday morning.

* WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 4 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 4 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling
people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting
in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of
drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without
warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks.
weather.instruction:
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf
conditions.

infrastructure. Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous surf
and NEVER turn your back on the ocean. Monitor local weather,
surf and tide forecasts at www.weather.gov/mtr.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 18 at 1:25AM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 10 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of northeast Florida, including the following areas, Coastal Duval, Coastal Flagler, Eastern Clay, Eastern Putnam, Inland Flagler, Northeast Coastal St. Johns, Northern Inland St. Johns, South Central Duval, Southeast Coastal St. Johns, Southern Inland St. Johns, Trout River, Western Clay, Western Duval, Western Putnam and Western St. Johns. * WHEN...Through Friday evening. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Several rounds of heavy rainfall are expected to repeatedly occur in the watch area through the end of the week. Repeated rounds of heavy rainfall will result in the potential for urban and small stream flooding for the coastal areas of northeast Florida. Total rainfall forecast through Friday night is around 3 to 8 inches with locally higher amounts up to 12 inches or more. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Winter Storm Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Heavy snow expected in the Eastern Sierra. For elevations between 5,000 and 8,000 feet, storm total snow accumulations of 10 to 18 inches expected. For elevations between 8,000 and 9,500 feet, storm total snow accumulations of 18 to 36 inches expected. Locally higher totals expected above 9,500 feet. Winds could gust as high as 55 mph. * WHERE...Eastern Sierra Slopes. * WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Friday. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. Widespread blowing snow could significantly reduce visibility. The hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday evening and Thursday morning commutes. Strong winds could cause extensive damage to trees and power lines. Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous. Whiteout conditions are expected and will make travel treacherous and potentially life-threatening.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by rain on snow is possible. * WHERE...Including the following area, SW Kenai Peninsula. This includes the cities of Homer, Anchor Point, Ninilchik, And Clam Gulch. * WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - An atmospheric river event is anticipated to begin Wednesday morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. With upslope enhancement, most areas are on track to see 2 to 3 inches of rainfall from this system, with locally higher amounts with elevation. Heaviest rainfall rates will occur between Wednesday afternoon and Thursday morning with about a quarter of an inch per 3 hour period. This amount of rainfall on the new snowpack may cause flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in low-lying and poor drainage areas, and cause ponding of water on roadways. Rainfall is on track to decrease Thursday. - Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: SW Kenai Peninsula

weather.headline: Flood Watch issued November 17 at 1:32PM AKST until November 19 at 6:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
weather.description:
* WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by rain on
snow is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following area, SW Kenai Peninsula. This
includes the cities of Homer, Anchor Point, Ninilchik, And Clam
Gulch.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An atmospheric river event is anticipated to begin Wednesday
morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. With
upslope enhancement, most areas are on track to see 2 to 3 inches
of rainfall from this system, with locally higher amounts with
elevation. Heaviest rainfall rates will occur between Wednesday
afternoon and Thursday morning with about a quarter of an inch
per 3 hour period. This amount of rainfall on the new snowpack
may cause flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in low-lying
and poor drainage areas, and cause ponding of water on roadways.
Rainfall is on track to decrease Thursday.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.
weather.areaDesc: SW Kenai Peninsula

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...Including the following area, Southern Kenai Mtns. This includes the city of Seward. * WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Flooding may occur in poor drainage areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - An atmospheric river event is anticipated to begin Wednesday morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. With upslope enhancement, most areas are on track to see 2 to 4 inches of rainfall from this system, with locally higher amounts with elevation. Rainfall rates of up to a quarter of an inch per hour are possible between 3PM Wednesday through 3PM Thursday. Southerly to southeasterly winds will shift to more easterly early Thursday morning, limiting precipitation amounts in lee of the mountains for areas along the Seward Highway from roughly Moose Pass and southward to Seward. Rainfall is on track to decrease late Thursday afternoon. Prolonged heavy rain may lead to areas of flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in low-lying and poor drainage areas, and ponding of water on roadways. - Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10- 18 feet, with local sets of 18 to 22 feet. Peak surf is expected from late tonight through Thursday night. Dangerous rip currents expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 3 AM to 10 AM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible, especially to Pismo and Cayucos piers. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Breaking waves may impact the Morro Bay Harbor. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding may continue through the secondary high tide in the evening. Additional hazardous surf and coastal flooding issues are expected next week.

counties.

to take action should flooding develop.

weather.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Flash Flood Watch
events.description: Between 3 to 6 inches of rain have fallen across the Santa Lucia Range impacting the Timber and Plaskett Fire Burn Scars over the last 24 hours. Expect additional rounds of scattered moderate to heavy rain impacting the Central Coast and Napa County through Thursday evening. * WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall continue to be possible over the Plaskett burn area and Timber burn area. * WHERE...For the Timber Scar, portions of CA Highway 1 and the Los Padres National Forecast from Andrew Molera State Park to Partington Ridge including the town of Big Sur. For the Plaskett Scar, areas near CA Highway 1 mile marker 17 to mile marker 11 including Los Burros Road. * WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas is expected during the watch period. Residents near the Timber burn area should prepare for potential debris flow moving through the drainages within Lafler, Castro, and Graves Canyons, as well as drainages between Grimes and Castro Canyons. Residents near the Plaskett burn area should prepare for potential debris flow moving through the Alder, Plaskett, and Prewitt Creeks. Be sure to stay up to date with information from local authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding of low-lying areas, roadway flooding, and debris flows in and near recent wildfire burn scars. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas, which may lead to flash flooding and debris flows. - Some locations that may experience flash flooding include... Big Sur, Plaskett, and Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County. .Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has caused the river near Cocoa to rise through Major Flood Stage and has now quickly passed record flood stage. Additional heavy rainfall over the next 48 hours will continue to produce river rises above record flood levels through late week and into this weekend. For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w, Above Lake Harney, Sanford, Deland, Astor...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. The forecast river level is above the all time flood of record. * WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage Fish Camp. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 1:15 PM EST Thursday the stage was 18.3 feet. - Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 1:15 PM EST Thursday was 18.3 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood stage at 18.3 feet. - Flood stage is 16.0 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

location.region: Brevard, FL

weather.headline: Flood Warning issued November 19 at 1:53PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Cocoa 9w affecting Brevard County.

.Extreme rainfall over the headwaters of the St. Johns River has
caused the river near Cocoa to rise through Major Flood Stage and has
now quickly passed record flood stage. Additional heavy rainfall over
the next 48 hours will continue to produce river rises above record
flood levels through late week and into this weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Cocoa 9w, Above Lake Harney,
Sanford, Deland, Astor...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
The forecast river level is above the all time flood of record.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Cocoa 9w.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 17.2 feet, Water enters homes along the St Johns River
in the Lake Poinsett area west of Cocoa, also low lying homes in
the Silver Pines subdivision in Rockledge and the Shakespeare Park
area of Cocoa. Providence Road area west of Cocoa becomes
impassable, cutting off access to homes in the Mullet Lane and Bass
Road area. Docks flooded and water in parking lot at Lone Cabbage
Fish Camp.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1:15 PM EST Thursday the stage was 18.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 1:15 PM EST Thursday was 18.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 18.3 feet.
- Flood stage is 16.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

To escape rising water, take the shortest path to higher ground.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Friday morning at 1000 AM EST.

weather.instruction:
Monitor the weather situation closely and be alert for threatening
weather conditions.

This storm may intensify, so be certain to monitor local radio
stations and available television stations for additional information
and possible warnings from the National Weather Service.

Frequent cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning can strike 10 miles away from a thunderstorm. Seek a safe
shelter inside a building or vehicle.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with these storms and may lead
to flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded
roadways.

* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet with dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa
Barbara County Southeastern Coast.

* WHEN...Until 3 AM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Pooling of sea
water is possible around high tide at beach and harbor areas
that is uncommon with normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach
erosion is also possible. No significant damage is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding may occur near
early morning high tide. Additional hazardous surf and coastal
flooding issues are expected next week.
weather.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.
weather.areaDesc: Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast

* WHERE...The Wasatch Mountains.

* IMPACTS...Winter driving conditions are expected. Roads, and

weather.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, and water in your
vehicle in case of an emergency. For winter road conditions from the
Utah Department of Transportation, visit
http://www.udottraffic.utah.gov.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

For graphical depictions of the snowfall forecast, including Official
NWS Forecast, High End Amount, and Low End Amount, visit
weather.gov/slc/winter.

events.title: Flood Warning
events.description: ...Forecast flooding changed from Moderate to Major severity for the following rivers in Florida... St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties. .On the St Johns River at Astor, the river is forecast to continue to rise through Moderate Flood Stage, reaching Major Flood Stage into early next week due to strong onshore flow causing a surge up the river as well as additional heavy rainfall expected across the basin. For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Major flooding is forecast. * WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast. * WHERE...St Johns River near Astor. * WHEN...Until further notice. * IMPACTS...At 4.0 feet, Major flooding occurs with water entering many structures on canals and along the river. Long duration flooding will occur, with levels taking weeks to months to return below flood stage. Water rescues will be necessary. River Road becomes inaccessible, with 1 to 2 feet water depth in numerous homes on Wildhog, Possum, Bonnet and Snail roads. Roads along Blue Creek are inaccessible with major flooding of homes on Otter, Branch and Chestnut roads. Camp South Moon Road and Juno Trail are inaccessible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 8:30 AM EST Thursday the stage was 3.2 feet. - Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet. - Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending at 8:30 AM EST Thursday was 3.2 feet. - Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 4.0 feet Monday morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter. - Flood stage is 2.3 feet. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Air Quality Alert
events.description: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection has issued a code ORANGE air quality alert for Thursday, for the Mon Valley area. Sensitive groups include children, the elderly, and people suffering from asthma, heart disease, or other lung diseases. The effects of air pollution can be minimized by avoiding outdoor exercise or strenuous activity. For more information on ground-level ozone and fine particles, visit http://www.airnow.gov and https://www.ahs.dep.pa.gov/AQPartnersWeb/

direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Avalanche Warning
events.description: AVWREV The following message is transmitted at the request of the U.S. Forest Service Sierra Avalanche Center. BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WARNING IMMEDIATE BROADCAST REQUESTED 05:30 PST Thu Nov 19 2026 The Sierra Avalanche Center in Truckee has issued a BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WARNING for the following areas: NWS Reno NV - NVZ002 (Greater Lake Tahoe)...CAZ072 (Greater Lake Tahoe (CA)) * WHAT...HIGH avalanche danger exists in the backcountry. Large avalanches are expected across backcountry terrain. * WHERE...Central Sierra Nevada Mountains between Yuba Pass (Hwy 49) on the north and Ebbetts Pass (Hwy 4) on the south, including the greater Lake Tahoe area. This applies only to backcountry areas, not to ski areas and highways where avalanche mitigation programs exist. * WHEN...In effect from Thu 05:30 PST to Fri 04:00 PST. * IMPACTS...Significant amounts of new snow and wind are creating dangerous avalanche conditions in the backcountry. The new snow is overloading a weak snowpack in some upper elevation areas. Avalanches could run down into treed terrain. * PRECAUTIONARY / PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...Very dangerous avalanche conditions exist in the backcountry. Traveling in, near, or below backcountry avalanche terrain is not recommended during HIGH avalanche danger. Consult https://www.sierraavalanchecenter.org/ or www.avalanche.org for more detailed information. Similar avalanche danger may exist at locations outside the coverage area of this or any avalanche center.

IMMEDIATE BROADCAST REQUESTED

05:30 PST Thu Nov 19 2026

exist.

overloading a weak snowpack in some upper elevation areas.

* PRECAUTIONARY / PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...Very dangerous avalanche
conditions exist in the backcountry. Traveling in, near, or below
backcountry avalanche terrain is not recommended during HIGH
avalanche danger.

for more detailed information.

Similar avalanche danger may exist at locations outside the coverage
area of this or any avalanche center.
